_meta.purpose: Version stamp and release notes, shown in the what changed sheet.
_meta.note: The version must mirror index.html's app-version meta tag; verify.mjs enforces it.

releases.head: Shorter, plainer words
changes: Every planning screen is rewritten in plain words that speak to you directly.
Short is the new default. Each move leads with what changes, and the reasons and dates are one tap away.
Switch to Detailed in Settings, or on the last setup step, to see everything in full.
About 4,300 words of old text that never showed on screen are gone.
The P6 page no longer shows an internal research note.

releases.head: Beatty's subjects first
changes: Set levels shows the subjects Beatty offers, at the levels Beatty runs them: Additional Mathematics and Principles of Accounts at G3, Design and Technology at G2, and so on.
Every other school's subjects are under More subjects, for a transfer or another school. A switch in Settings shows the full list.
Advice only suggests a subject and level Beatty runs. Music and Computing at G3 are marked as taken at another school or centre.
In Sec 1 and 2, G1 Humanities is named for what it is: the Humanities Exposure Modules.
Subject names are spelt out in full, such as Humanities (Social Studies, Geography) and Science (Physics, Chemistry).

releases.head: Advice that fits the year
changes: Sec 1 and Sec 2 are judged by their own rules, in the subjects I take now. The five subject counts belong to the SEC, so they no longer show up as moves in lower secondary.
In Sec 1 and Sec 2, places read On track instead of Open: nothing opens before the SEC. Each place says once what the SEC will count.
Mother Tongue no longer has to be G3 for Junior College or Millennia Institute in lower secondary advice, matching the 2028 rules.
Moves say what they lead to in Sec 3, such as G3 Maths and Additional Maths, and that the school sets the mark and decides.
P6: a list of the choices my PSLE gives me and what each puts on track, a place for a Higher Mother Tongue result, and the Foundation option for Posting Group 3.
SEC rules re-checked: a third Humanities, Maths or Science at G3 for JC and MI, four at G3 for NAFA and LASALLE, and grade targets that apply each place's own rules.

releases.head: Clearer words, readable at night
changes: Every button and label is now readable in dark mode. Text on coloured fills follows the theme, and a new check stops white text on light fills from coming back.
The four places are now Home, Subjects, Pathways and Saved.
The tabs say what you do: Set levels, Best moves, Grade targets, Year guide.
Distance in moves: Open now, 1 to 2 moves away, 3 to 5 moves away, or Another route in.
Clearer place names: Sec 5, NAFA or LASALLE, Higher Nitec (2 yrs) and Higher Nitec (3 yrs).
Buttons name their action: Save move, Copy words, Skip setup, Copy your Sec 2 levels into Sec 3. The header shows who is reading: I am: Student.

releases.head: Year by year
changes: A page for every year, P6 to Sec 5, on one transit line you can tap along.
Advice that names the move: which subject, which level, and what it opens.
Targets: enter the grades you expect and aim for, and see the scores each place reads.
My plan: one page for the next conversation, voiced for a student, a parent or a teacher.
The admission rules for 2028 re-checked, with the course families behind an option.
A new look: the night line. Navy and signal yellow, a departures board that answers every tap, advice as tickets you keep, and your score drawn as a train on a track.
A guided start: a short wordless intro, then four steps to your first move. Home now shows one next step.

releases.head: A new map
changes: The map is now the whole tool: it is the home screen, it answers every subject you tap in Plan, it grows as you play, and it is the card you keep at the end.
The back button works everywhere, and a reload puts you back where you were.
First visit asks your year and your guess once, then never again.
The rulebook now arrives in three steps: a plain word, a plain sentence, and the exact rule with its source behind one fold.
Money, work and your school now appear where they matter, not only as pages.
One face for the words on every phone, and dark mode is a proper night.
